identity.name: parcels
identity.description: Loads Toronto's Property Boundaries CSV (~498K rows, ~224 MB, GeoJSON `geometry` column) from the CKAN Open Data portal into the parcels table: a class-A guarded upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (parcel_id) DO UPDATE ... WHERE <9 IS DISTINCT FROM terms>, NO retraction anywhere) over 17 columns + geom, in one step-scoped transaction. DEFAULT codegen authors the statement (plan D1 REVISED, operator ruling 2026-09-24) via two DECLARED axes — `columns[].on_empty:"preserve"|"preserve_null"` (prerequisites 0m/0m-follow-on) and `outputs.invalidates[].set_null_on_change_of` (prerequisite 0l) — so the legacy SET text (the five COALESCE(NULLIF(...)) address preservations, the date_effective COALESCE, and the three DEC-FENCE2 CASE arms) is reproduced by the shared library, never a per-step compute-authored statement. The INGESTOR archetype's THIRD member (after load_ravines class B and address_points class A); first row converted under R-PACE-1's compressed form.

why_lock.text: Mutual exclusion with every other writer of parcels across the fleet (Spec 47 §A.5 lock registry row 55) [READ scripts/load-parcels.js:218, `const ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 55;`]. The lock is declared here and acquired by the library from descriptor.identity.lock; scripts/load-parcels.js keeps `const ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 55;` as a §5.4 SOURCE-TEXT constant (declared, never read), and the two are asserted equal by src/tests/steps/parcels/violations.test.ts. The lock holds across the whole step — acquisition, parse, the write and the score — because the ~498K-row load must not interleave with a second writer.

why.text: Class A, DEFAULT codegen (plan D1 REVISED, operator ruling 2026-09-24 — standardized/observable/scalable/simple: compute-authored SQL for the whole target is exactly what the ruling rejects for an INGESTOR [READ scripts/steps/_schema/step.schema.json:1054]). The pre-conversion loader issued ONE statement shape — INSERT INTO parcels (...) VALUES ... ON CONFLICT (parcel_id) DO UPDATE SET ... WHERE <9 OR-terms> IS DISTINCT FROM, NO DELETE anywhere (0 grep matches for DELETE/TRUNCATE) [READ scripts/load-parcels.js:297-378]. A byte-identical re-run updates zero rows; no parcel is ever removed by this step. Two DECLARED axes (prerequisites 0l/0m, executed by the shared codegen in scripts/lib/step/write.js) reproduce the legacy text without a line of step-specific SQL: `columns[].on_empty:"preserve"` on the five address columns (COALESCE(NULLIF(EXCLUDED.x,''), parcels.x)) + `"preserve_null"` on date_effective (COALESCE(EXCLUDED.x, parcels.x), the non-text NULLIF-less form), and `outputs.invalidates[].set_null_on_change_of:"geometry"` on the three DEC-FENCE2 stamps (the CASE...THEN NULL...END arms). This `guard_columns` list is EIGHT entries — the nine-term WHERE clause's ninth term, `parcels.geometry::jsonb IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.geometry::jsonb`, is NOT declared here: it is added automatically, FIRST, by the codegen because `geometry` is the watched column of all three `invalidates[]` entries below (deduplicated against this list — `changeOfGuardColumns` in write.js). geom is NOT itself a guard predicate: it is set unconditionally beside geometry whenever the guard passes. The reproduction is PROVEN, not asserted: step-library.logic.test.ts T5/T7 clone this exact shape (five on_empty:"preserve" columns + one preserve_null + three set_null_on_change_of:"geometry" entries + these eight guard_columns) and assert `buildWritePlan(...).upsertSqlFor(1)` equals the legacy file text whitespace-normalised; this descriptor's own violations.test.ts T7-cite fence re-proves it against THIS descriptor. The legacy script wrapped each 1,000-row batch in its OWN withTransaction (:252-253, :275); the library wraps ALL batches in ONE step-scoped transaction (executeWrite) — declared here as the truth, with the atomicity-window widening recorded in deviations[].

why.text: Exactly ONE write statement reaches parcels: the guarded upsert. There is NO departure DELETE (class A, retract none) and no staging replace, so the converted step's write inventory equals the pre-conversion one's single statement (which the legacy script issued once per 1,000-row batch inside its own per-batch transaction). The three invalidates[] entries below are NOT additional statements — they are lineage stamps NULLed by CASE arms INSIDE that same DO UPDATE.

RLS default-deny on the parcels family means the guarded upsert works ONLY because the pipeline role has rolbypassrls=true; under a non-bypass role the INSERT ... ON CONFLICT affects 0 rows with NO error, so the counters read 0, the verdict reads PASS and the run is indistinguishable from an unchanged source. The write is a bare INSERT ... DO UPDATE, unconditional at the row level; the bypass is the precondition, declared fail-loud.

The GiST index on parcels.geom (migration 039:21, replayed at 083:106) that every downstream spatial join in the chain plans through — link-parcels, compute-centroids, the enrich-* steps, and the DEC-FENCE2 consumers. Without it those joins degrade to sequential scans over ~486K parcels. Declared fail-loud because the write path itself populates geom and a missing index silently converts the chain's spatial work into heap scans.

on_row_error_why.text: A source row the step refuses to carry is counted and the load continues: FEATURE_TYPE CORRIDOR/RESERVE (:487), an expired non-sentinel DATE_EXPIRY (:495) and an empty PARCELID (:500) each `continue`, and a row that yields no dimensions still loads with null frontage/depth. The tolerance is bounded by the declared skip_rate_pct check below; no bare percentage literal survives here (Rule 3).

on_batch_error_why.text: PR-D1 (PIN, DO NOT FIX — Spec 123 §3.1, review_followups #68). A failed flushBatch() logs, `errors++`, and DROPS the batch's rows for the run [READ scripts/load-parcels.js:550-554; the same in the truncated-CSV recovery path :571-575], and records_unchanged is then inflated by the dropped count [:401's own comment]. The conversion carries that behaviour as-is and DECLARES it here rather than silently reshaping it; fail_step would be a behaviour change smuggled into a no-op-diff commit. The post-cutover fix, if any, is a separate commit with its own RED lock.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check here reads a value the library already measured (missing CSV header columns, null-address rows, skipped rows, the rows-read total, the geometry-parse fallback count), so a check that throws is a library defect, not an upstream condition — it must redden the run rather than drop its row.

why.text: Spec 79 CRIT-3b (loader :470-478 + scripts/lib/parcels-csv-drift.js detectMissingColumns). The loader surfaces a REQUIRED_CSV_COLUMNS loss in its OWN audit table so an operator who runs the chain past a failing assert_schema still sees it. A header that drops `geometry` silently strips geom from every row while the counts still look healthy, so the drift is its own WARN row. Reused from the drift lib, never forked; the lib's own 0.10 literal is untouched by this conversion (it is assert-schema's fingerprint input).

expect.of: rows with an empty ADDRESS_NUMBER over rows attempted

why.text: PR-D2 (PIN, DO NOT FIX — Spec 123 §3.1; review_followups:156 stays ACT, its own WF3). buildNullAddressAuditRow (parcels-csv-drift.js:73-77) + loader :424. The row is STRUCTURALLY UNSATISFIABLE as PASS since the 2026-05-20 strip: the CSV no longer carries ADDRESS_NUMBER at all, so the fraction is ~100% and the row reads WARN on EVERY run. The conversion carries it as-is and declares the unsatisfiability in limitations[]; retiring the check would HIDE the strip from a future reader, which is the opposite of the observability the row exists to provide. No limit_from_config: the 0.10 boundary is the drift lib's own literal, and peeling it here would force an assert_schema golden recapture (that lib is assert-schema.descriptor.json's fingerprint input).

A rising skip rate signals CSV drift [READ load-parcels.js:421, `{ metric: 'skip_rate', ... status: skipRate >= 10 ? 'FAIL' : 'PASS' }`]. A row is skipped on FEATURE_TYPE CORRIDOR/RESERVE (:487), an expired non-sentinel DATE_EXPIRY (:495) or an empty PARCELID (:500). FAIL-severity EXACTLY as the legacy reads — this row is genuinely legacy FAIL, unlike rows_read_floor below (which stays WARN and must NOT be promoted). blocking:false (PIN, DO NOT FIX): a FAIL row today exits 0 and the chain continues. Bound externalized to parcels_skip_rate_max_pct (Rule 3).

Catastrophic-load detector [READ load-parcels.js:416, `threshold: '>= 450000', status: processed < 450000 ? 'WARN' : 'PASS'`]. SEVERITY STAYS WARN — the address_points AP-D5 lesson is severity is NOT archetype-derived; this legacy row warns and promoting it would introduce a halt that never existed. The bound SHARES the registered variable `sources_parcels_floor` (Spec 43/44; scripts/seeds/logic_variables.json, default 460000) through limit_from_config — the SAME key assert_data_bounds declares, not a second one (Rule 3, one home per concern). PR-D5 (PINNED, §5.1): the loader's own 450000 WARN threshold and the registered 460000 FAIL floor disagree by 10,000 rows; unifying them is a DATA-POLICY ruling Spec 123 §3.1 forbids folding into a zero-diff conversion, so the delta is recorded in limitations[]. The `limit` string uses verdict.js's R-T addendum `value_min` form (a RAW MEASURED value), NOT `"viol == 0"` — the exact AP-D6 trap where resolveLimit substitutes the config value into the string and compares a 0/1 violation flag against ~460000, making the check FAIL unconditionally on every run.

Zero-tolerance invariant [READ load-parcels.js:422, `{ metric: 'records_errors', threshold: '== 0', status: errors > 0 ? 'FAIL' : 'PASS' }`]. `errors` is incremented only by the batch-drop path (PR-D1) and the truncated-CSV flush failure, so a nonzero reading means rows were dropped — the exact condition PR-D1 pins. FAIL-severity, blocking:false (PIN, DO NOT FIX). A raw violation count, so `viol == 0` is the correct form here (no limit_from_config).

expect.reports: source rows whose `geometry` value would not JSON.parse, counted not gated

why.text: parseGeoJSON's `try { JSON.parse } catch { return null }` (:169-176) refuses to surface an unparseable geometry, and NOTHING downstream `continue`s on it — the row IS carried with a null geometry/geojson (mirroring address_points' own AP-D2 swallow). The conversion carries the swallow VERBATIM and turns it into a counted, declared row. INFO is legal HERE ONLY because this is purely DESCRIPTIVE: it has no negative direction, it cannot reach WARN/FAIL, and it never gates. The declaration is the close — a promoted WARN would be a behaviour change.

expect.reports: rows the compute's shapeRecord refused to carry (feature-type / expiry / empty key)

why.text: The runner's shaped_skipped counter (Spec 122 §5.1 ingress seam) — the number of source records the step declined to carry into rows, i.e. the legacy `skipped++` paths at :487/:495/:500. Purely descriptive (INFO, no negative direction), so a healthy run shows a counted zero where the pre-conversion `skipped++` could not: silence used to mean both 'zero' and 'nobody looked'.

deviations.from: the pre-conversion per-batch transaction shape (`pipeline.withTransaction` once per 1,000-row BATCH_SIZE batch, :252-253, :275)

why.text: Plan D1 (orchestrator-ruled). The library's executeWrite wraps ALL insert batches in ONE step-scoped withTransaction; `execution.txn_scope` therefore declares `step` (the truth). The widening is an ATOMICITY-WINDOW change: today a mid-run failure leaves the already-committed batches persisted (partial load); converted, the run is all-or-nothing. It is NOT a success-path change — a successful run writes byte-identical rows, which is what the POST golden proves. The single-txn duration + WAL for ~486K rows is MEASURED at ② capture (plan D1); if the measurement breaches the step budget, this deviation is re-adjudicated before ③. Address_points precedent: same declaration, same reason.

deviations.from: the `process.argv[2]` local-path override (:228) and the data/property-boundaries-4326.csv fs.existsSync download-vs-cache short-circuit (:230-236)

why.text: Retired per Spec 124 R-AZ (the argv-seam rule). A debug affordance let an operator run against a hand-supplied local CSV without downloading; the frozen shell reads no argv (the §5.1 shape forbids it) and the fixture tier replaces it for tests. The CACHE half is retired with it: leaving an existsSync short-circuit implicit would let a STALE local CSV silently feed a run, so `inputs.reads.externals[0].cache:"none"` records that the local file was never a revalidated artifact and the step re-downloads every run (the load_ravines / address_points posture).

deviations.adjudicated_by: orchestrator ruling, Spec 124 R-AZ / plan D2

deviations.from: the legacy download/parse progress-cadence literals (`10 * 1024 * 1024` download window :181, `processed % 50000 === 0` progress modulo :556, `484000` progress denominator :557)

why.text: RETIRED, dead under the whole-array model (plan D3). The pre-conversion script streamed the CSV row-by-row and logged a progress line every 50,000 processed rows against a 484,000-row denominator (itself STALE vs the 498,479 actual rows); the converted INGESTOR runner's CSV acquisition path hands off the WHOLE parsed array in one step and logs a single 'acquired N feature(s)' line. There is no per-byte or per-row progress loop left for a cadence tunable to bind to, so declaring one would be a dead operator-facing knob (the address_points commit-9 P4 precedent). Retired rather than forced onto a fabricated consumer.

deviations.adjudicated_by: orchestrator ruling, plan D3 (address_points commit-9 P4 precedent)

deviations.from: declaring `guards.requires` only for what the write/consumers need, and pinning every FAIL check as blocking:false

why.text: PR-D1/D2/D3/D4 posture (PIN, DO NOT FIX — Spec 123 §3.1). Today every terminal of this step exits 0: pipeline.run discards the return value, run-chain records the FAIL verdict and folds it into chain status completed_with_errors, and the chain CONTINUES. blocking:true would make the library throw after the emit and halt the sources chain — a real behaviour change smuggled into a commit whose whole claim is that it changes nothing. Promoting a check is its own peel with its own lock. Likewise guards.requires declares ONLY the parcels GIST index and the RLS bypass the write path needs — not every index the table carries.

deviations.adjudicated_by: orchestrator ruling, plan D4 / address_points plan D-8

limitations.what: PR-D2 — the `null_address_pct` check is STRUCTURALLY UNSATISFIABLE as PASS: Toronto Open Data stripped ADDRESS_NUMBER (and LINEAR_NAME_FULL, DATE_EFFECTIVE) from the Property Boundaries CSV between 2026-05-19 and 2026-05-20, so nullAddressCount/attemptedRows is ~100% and the row reads WARN on EVERY run. Declared as a check at WARN severity and carried as-is; the check is deliberately NOT retired, because retiring it would hide the strip from a future reader. review_followups:156 stays ACT (its own WF3).
limitations.measured: load-parcels.js:424 → buildNullAddressAuditRow(nullAddressCount, attemptedRows); parcels-csv-drift.js:73-77; the strip's Day-1 COALESCE defence is the 5-preservation block at load-parcels.js:326-330 [MEASURED 2026-09-24, report §5.1 PR-D2]

limitations.what: PR-D5 — the load floor is declared TWICE with two different numbers. The loader WARNs below 450,000 (:416); the registered `sources_parcels_floor` seed FAILs below 460,000. A run reading 455,000 rows therefore reads PASS on the loader's own audit table and FAIL on assert_data_bounds, so the loader's check cannot see the fleet's real floor. PINNED, not unified: unifying the number is a DATA-POLICY change (which number is right?) that Spec 123 §3.1 forbids folding into a zero-diff conversion. Its own followup.
limitations.measured: load-parcels.js:416 `>= 450000` WARN vs scripts/seeds/logic_variables.json:5050-5058 `sources_parcels_floor` default 460000 FAIL [MEASURED 2026-09-24, report §6]

limitations.what: PR-D3 — CKAN coordinate jitter (review_followups:3075): the published polygon vertices drift at the sub-metre level between CKAN publishes with no version/etag change, so `geometry::jsonb IS DISTINCT FROM` fires on rows whose data did not meaningfully change. Carried as-is. Consequence: the DEC-FENCE2 stamps are NULLed (and the enrich-* steps recompute) for jitter-only rows, and the golden's byte-identity claim is per-run, not per-source-publish.
limitations.measured: review_followups:3075; the guard's first disjunct at load-parcels.js:362 [MEASURED 2026-09-24, report §5.1 PR-D3]

limitations.what: PR-D4 — centroid invalidation gap (review_followups:3114): compute-centroids' derived centroid is NOT in the DEC-FENCE2 invalidate list, so a moved parcel keeps a stale centroid until compute_centroids is forced full. Named and explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this conversion — it is a compute_centroids defect, and compute_centroids is already converted.
limitations.measured: compute-centroids.js has no `*_when_enriched` stamp to NULL; the three DEC-FENCE2 arms at load-parcels.js:353-361 name ravine, heritage and centreline only [MEASURED 2026-09-24, report §5.1 PR-D4]

limitations.what: Class-A non-retraction: because the loader never retracts, a `parcel_id` can only vanish from parcels via a source-side change the class-A shape cannot express. The ordering guarantee 'parcels before link-parcels / compute-centroids / enrich-*' (Spec 43 row 5) is unaffected, but a parcel deleted upstream stays in the table with its last-seen values.

PR-D1 residue — a failed batch's rows are logged, counted in `errors`, and DROPPED for the run, so the load can complete with fewer than the source's rows and no per-row evidence of which; `records_unchanged` is inflated by the dropped count. Declared via execution.on_batch_error:"drop_batch".
limitations.measured: load-parcels.js:550-554 (catch → log.error, errors++, batch = []) and :401's own 'lost rows inflate this count' comment [MEASURED 2026-09-24, report §5.1 PR-D1]

limitations.what: The PostGIS-absent arm, SUPERSEDED by plan D1 REVISED: the legacy script probed pg_extension for postgis (:239-241) and set `geomLine = ''` when absent (:293-296), so on a PostGIS-less database parcels.geometry was written while parcels.geom stayed NULL, with no audit row naming the divergence. The converted step has NO equivalent runtime branch — DEFAULT codegen's `geom` column (bind:"wkb_geometry") unconditionally renders `ST_GeomFromWKB`, and `guards.requires` above already declares the `idx_parcels_geom_gist` index fail-loud on_missing — a PostGIS-less database fails the guard BEFORE acquisition rather than silently degrading to a geometry-only write. This is a genuine behaviour change from silent-degrade to fail-loud, judged consistent with the guard's own stated posture ("declared fail-loud") rather than a new divergence to hide.
limitations.measured: load-parcels.js:239-241 (pg_extension probe, legacy) and :293-296 (geomLine conditional, legacy) [READ 2026-09-24; report §1.2 and §R LOW-CONFIDENCE #4]; scripts/lib/step/write.js default codegen has no hasPostGIS branch [READ 2026-09-24, row 3.7 ② D1 REVISED]

limitations.what: The skip_rate_pct and rows_read_floor bounds are compared against THIS run's numbers only; there is no vs-prior-run trend check. A source that shrinks 40% but stays above the floor reads as a healthy load.
limitations.measured: load-parcels.js:415-424 — auditRows read only this run's processed/inserted/updated/skipped/errors counters [MEASURED 2026-09-24, report §1.5]

interrupted_why.text: Rule 12 truthful posture. This step is class A (`guarded_upsert`, retract:"none"): it has NO retraction path and NO scoped delete, so a kill mid-run leaves exactly what the step-scoped transaction left — either nothing (rolled back) or the fully-committed guarded upsert. There is no half-cleared table an incremental gate could misread as complete, and no force_full_on_next_run obligation (that rule binds retract_when full_only or retract:"all" targets, neither of which exists here). Nothing is owed to a successor run beyond re-running the idempotent upsert, which zero-writes on a byte-identical source.

before_image_why.text: The generic before-image mechanism mirrors a retraction's write_discipline.scope predicate as a SELECT — it structurally requires a scope. This step declares retract:"none" with write_discipline.scope:"none": there is no retraction for the mechanism to mirror, so there is nothing to capture. Every column is re-derived from the source on every run, so a re-run recovers identically without a before-image. Genuinely out of scope rather than silently ignored.

why.text: The guarded upsert committed: rows_read parsed, inserted/updated split by RETURNING (xmax = 0), no retraction. The step has no staleness gate, so success is the NORMAL terminal every run.

A declared WARN check tripped (csv_header_drift, null_address_pct or rows_read_floor) with no FAIL. PR-D2 makes this the common case today: the null-address WARN stands on every run. The load still happened because none of these makes the data unloadable.
skip_rate_pct or records_errors reached FAIL — a rising skip rate or a dropped batch. The FAIL row is declared; blocking:false (PIN, DO NOT FIX) so the run is `failed` and the chain continues.

The download or the CSV parse threw (a fatal parse error rethrows at :580-582, unlike address_points). The temp file is removed on this path exactly as on every other, and no write has been attempted.
inputs.expect_nonempty is true: a source that parses to ZERO records fails rather than landing an empty 'success' — an empty CSV is a publisher error, not an empty load.

Advisory lock 55 is held by another process. Pre-conversion the step wrapped everything in pipeline.withAdvisoryLock and returned silently when the lock was not acquired; the library now emits a row-derived SKIP summary.
